pages.why: 9 plain [ID] ceiling-text-floor requirements, balanced ceilings/floors - the ordinary case, at density
5 requirements of which 2 are titled (SWS_Can_91019, SWS_Can_91020); both titled bodies are tables, the awkward case for text extraction. Also carries hyphen-split upstream ids (SRS_BSW_-\n00369)
SWS_Can_00407 opens here and closes on page 35 - the page-break case (7 ceilings, 6 floors). Pairs with can_driver_p035; only meaningful together
closes SWS_Can_00407 (7 ceilings, 8 floors). The page furniture between the two halves is exactly what the cleaning pass has to remove
section 6 Requirements Tracing SRS->SWS table: must yield ZERO requirements. The false-positive guard
7 plain requirements in the other ID casing (SWS_CANIF_* versus SWS_Can_*). Both documents must be represented or a casing bug passes every test
SWS_Can_CONSTR_00509/00510/00511 - the _CONSTR_ infix. Omitting the infix from the id pattern silently drops ~20 requirements across the corpus and nothing else here would catch it

the fifth document (SWS_CanNm_*): two titled 'Definition of API function ... ⌈<table>⌋' requirements whose bodies are whole service tables, interleaved with plain one-sentence requirements; SWS_CanNm_00213 closes with '⌋() ()' — a stray extra empty parens pair after the upstream list

the COM document at density: 6 self-contained requirements — 5 plain + the titled 'Definition of configurable interface' table variant — every one with an upstream (SRS_Com_02037), a cross-module PduR_ComTransmit symbol, and ComIPdu* config parameters that must not be extracted as symbols

the PDU Router casing quirk: [SWS_PDUR_00816] — the document's only UPPERCASE-spelled id, genuine in the source — sits next to the normally-cased [SWS_PduR_00100]; both are titled table-body requirements carrying the spec's own 'Definiton' typo, one with SRS_BSW upstream refs and one with an empty ⌋()
